Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund distributed automatically to the approximately 400,000 identifiable members, plus up to $7 million in court-approved fees and expenses. We are not seeking a claims process or a provision returning unawarded fees to Brightline. Please let us know your response, including any concerns about the fund or fee request.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Thank you for the proposal. We agree that automatic payments to identifiable members are preferable to a claims process, and we do not seek a return of unawarded fees. The $43 million combined amount exceeds our settlement authority. We propose a $32 million class fund and up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any reduction in the fee award going to the class. We would retain the ability to address the fee request before the court.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $32 million class fund distributed automatically, up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class rather than Brightline.

private_notes.private_reasoning: An opening proposal should prioritize meaningful, automatic class recovery and avoid terms that could divert value from members or undermine approval. A $36 million fund exceeds the unadjusted $27.5 million trial expected value, but reflects a reasonable opening position rather than a bottom line. A separately paid $7 million fee is subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class.

The proposed $43 million total exceeds Brightline’s $40 million authority. A counteroffer with automatic distribution, no fee reversion, and no clear-sailing provision preserves approval prospects while leaving room to negotiate.

The $32 million automatic class fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial expected recovery before certification risk and delay. The $6 million fee remains subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. Accepting secures substantial class relief without introducing problematic claims or reversion terms.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Hargrove Lane LLP proposed a $36 million class fund with automatic payments to identifiable members, together with up to $7 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $32 million class fund and up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, which we accepted. The parties discussed class relief and fees together; class relief was not agreed upon before fees were discussed. The settlement has no clear-sailing provision. Any fees the court does not award will go to the class, not Brightline. The court and class members will receive the complete negotiation transcript. We recognize that negotiating relief and fees together warrants scrutiny, and the fee request remains subject to the court’s independent approval.
